Based on the healthcare Q&A matches provided, it appears that follow-up recommendations for abnormal Papanicolaou (Pap) smear results can have a significant impact on patient adherence to recommended actions.

Prompt: Do follow-up recommendations for abnormal Papanicolaou smears influence patient adherence?

Completion: Adherence to follow-up was low in this family planning clinic population, no matter what type of follow-up was advised. Adherence was improved by the use of up to 3 reminders. Allocating resources to effective methods for improving adherence to follow-up of abnormal results may be more important than which follow-up procedure is recommended.

In other words, following up with patients who have had abnormal Pap smears and providing them with regular reminders can lead to better adherence to recommended actions, such as scheduling a follow-up appointment or making any necessary medical interventions. This suggests that the effectiveness of these recommendations should be prioritized over the type of recommendation being made (e.g., which specific procedure to use for follow-up).
